subject: AcmeHealth GDPR: DPA & SCC module selection - next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example>
To: Sara Connor <sara.connor@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.example>
Date: 2027-02-20T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: AcmeHealth GDPR: DPA & SCC module selection - next steps

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the sync earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum on legal/compliance: 

What we covered
- Acme Health will be the data controller for patient and PII records; Redwood will act as a processor for inference/embeddings.
- You asked about our DPA and which SCC (Standard Contractual Clauses) module we recommend for cross-border transfers.
- We confirmed Redwood has SOC 2 Type II (in scope) and we can provide the report under NDA; Neha will own the delivery.

Attachments I’m sending
- Redwood_DPA_template_v2.pdf — our standard DPA with optional SCC slots
- SCC-module-options.xlsx — short note on Module 1 vs Module 2 tradeoffs (controller/processor alignment)

Proposed next steps
1) Please confirm that Acme intends to remain the controller for customer-facing data, and whether you prefer Module 1 (Controller-to-Processor) or Module 2 (Processor-to-Processor) SCCs. Based on our conversation, Module 2 may be the closer fit if you have sub-processor relationships, but want to confirm.
2) Tom/legal: if helpful, complete the short questionnaire (we can ingest answers into our vendor security questionnaire). I’ve attached the SCC options for quick comparison.
3) Neha will follow up with a SOC 2 delivery plan and a redline-friendly DPA that highlights the SCC selection.
4) Target: get legal alignment and DocuSign-ready DPA by Fri, 2027-02-26.

If that timeline works, I’ll create a HubSpot task and route the DocuSign link once you confirm module selection.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround here.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.example | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment stubs: Redwood_DPA_template_v2.pdf (PDF, 145 KB); SCC-module-options.xlsx (Excel, 12 KB)

From: Sara Connor <sara.connor@acmehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example>
Cc: Tom Baker <tom.baker@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>
Date: 2027-02-21T09:22:00+00:00
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth GDPR: DPA & SCC module selection - next steps

Hi Rishi + team —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the following from Acme’s side: 
- Acme Health will remain the controller for patient/PII data.
- Initial preference is Module 2 SCCs (Processor-to-Processor) because our workflows involve multiple processors and we want those obligations captured end-to-end.
- We’d like to see the SOC 2 Type II report; Tom and legal will complete the questionnaire you mentioned.

Next actions for us
- I’ll have Tom fill out the security questionnaire and send it back by EOD Thu (attached once complete).
- Legal: we’ll review your DPA and revert with any redlines. If you can flag the SCC clause you recommend for Module 2 that will speed review.

Timeline: We’re aiming to have procurement sign-off for tooling by the end of next week, so the 2027-02-26 target for a DocuSign-ready DPA works if we can get the annotated DPA this week.

Thanks — Sara
Sara Connor | Director, Product Operations
Acme Health
sara.connor@acmehealth.com | +44 20 7123 4567

Attachment stubs: (incoming) Acme_Security_Questionnaire_filled.xlsx (will send once Tom completes)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example>
To: Sara Connor <sara.connor@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.example>, Tom Baker <tom.baker@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-02-22T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth GDPR: DPA & SCC module selection - next steps

Great — thanks for the quick confirmation, Sara.

Notes from our legal side (internal): Neha has confirmed we can provision a DPA that defaults to Module 2 SCC language and we will: 
- Mark the SCC selection clearly in the DPA (redline-friendly clause).
- Provide a SOC 2 Type II summary and the full report under NDA (Neha will coordinate).

Attached: I’m sending an updated DPA that highlights Module 2 as the chosen SCC option. I also added a brief callout on subprocessors and data flow mapping that Acme asked about. If legal prefers different language we can iterate quickly — our legal team typically turns redlines around in 48 hours for enterprise deals.

Next steps (our side):
- Neha to deliver SOC 2 delivery plan + NDA link by 2027-02-23.
- I’ll upload the DocuSign envelope once you confirm no additional commercial changes.

Quick ask for Tom/legal: when you send the filled questionnaire please flag any controls where you want deeper evidence (e.g., key management, encryption at rest, retention). We can prioritize evidence packs for those items.

Thanks — will follow up with the DocuSign link.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: Redwood_DPA_template_v2.pdf (updated, PDF, 165 KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.example>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example>
Cc: Sara Connor <sara.connor@acmehealth.com>, Tom Baker <tom.baker@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-02-24T09:10:00-05:00
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth GDPR: DPA & SCC module selection - next steps

Looping in a quick legal/compliance note for the record.

1) SOC 2: Redwood has a current SOC 2 Type II report covering our inference platform and telemetry pipeline; we will provide the report under the attached NDA. I’ll drop the NDA link to Sara today and route the report via secure file share.

2) DPA / SCC: I reviewed the updated DPA — marking Module 2 as agreed for now. A couple of small redline suggestions I’ll add in-track: 
   - Narrow the subprocessors clause to require notice + 10 business day objection window for new subprocessors handling EU personal data.
   - Add a short retention table (we have a standard 30/90/365 options) for your procurement to pick.

3) Evidence packs: If Tom flags KM (key management) or encryption controls as priority we’ll package the templates for quick review.

I’ll upload the NDA and SOC 2 package to the secure share by EOD and will circulate a DocuSign-ready DPA after I fold in the two small edits above.

Best —
Neha Kapoor | Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.example
